units.translation: Scaliger thought βᾶ [O king] was used for βασιλεῦ [O king]. The scholiast who renders it ὦ πάτερ Ζεῦ, Γῆς παῖ [O father Zeus, child of Earth] seems to have read ὦ παῖ Γᾶς, πᾶ Ζεῦ [O child of Earth, father Zeus], as Valckenaer pointed out in his note on Theocritus' Adoniazusae p. 382, or ὦ πᾶ, Γᾶς παῖ, Ζεῦ [O father, child of Earth, Zeus], which others preferred. Arcadius p. 125, 14 records βᾶς, πᾶς πᾶ, ὁ πατήρ [father], and Choeroboscus p. 16, 8 records both (for whom Bâs is the proper name of a Pontic king, mentioned by Memnon in Photius' Bibliotheca p. 228, 17). But βᾶ used for βασιλεῦ [O king] is to be compared with similar examples of apocope, which Lobeck discussed in Paralipomena p. 78.
O king (βὰ M), child of Earth, Zeus.
O father Zeus, child of Earth
O child of Earth, father Zeus
O father, child of Earth, Zeus
and foot soldiers, advancing step by step, presenting a dense array of war.
like a spider, step by step.
they speak arrogant words against the city.
he speaks many words against the might of Tydeus with evil intent.
for the people have been released to speak freely.
they sleep in vain; I speak words that accomplish nothing.
and the dark depths around Tartarus.
before seeing the depth of evils.
It is thought to mean foundation in the corrupt passage Suppl. 860, which see under βαθυχαῖος [deep-noble].
and the statues of the gods have been uprooted and overturned from their bases in utter confusion.
O queen, highest of the deep-girdled Persian women.
Of what man or deep-girdled maiden?
to send forth grief from deep-bosomed breasts,
to the deep meadow of Lerna.
reaping a deep furrow through his mind.
bearing witness to a deep fall for me.
a city enclosed by a deep device of towers.
there is need of deep thought for safety.

The scholiast interprets the manifestly corrupt reading as ἡ μεγάλως εὐγενῆς · χάοι [the greatly noble; for the noble are called χάοι], (write χαοί) γὰρ οἱ εὐγενεῖς, ἐγὼ ή βαθυχαῖος ἀναξία ταύτης τῆς βαθρείας, ὦ γέρον [for the noble are called χάοι; I, the deep-noble, unworthy of this foundation, old man]. For βαθυχαῖος [deep-noble], unless this too is corrupt, βαθυχάϊος [deep-noble] should be written, with L. Dindorf in the Thesaurus vol. 2 p. 39, as χάϊος [noble] and χαϊώτερος [more noble] are written: on which see the Thesaurus vol. 8 p. 1222.

I, a rustic (γεῖος Hermannus, meaning possessor of land and born in it, γέγειος Lobeck in Paralipomena p. 552, ἔγγαιος Weilius) (ἔχω Butlerus), deep-noble, of the foundation, of the foundation, old man.
